Header: Fusarium oxysporium f.sp.cubense keelay ka Panama

Prevention: Use suckers or rhizomes from healthy plants for planting.
Avoid planting on fields with a history of this disease.
Avoid movement of infected material to uninfected areas.
Provide good draining facilities as this disease is more severe in poorly drained soils.
Avoid runoff water from diseased areas as fungus can be spread by the water.
Sterilize working tools after handling diseased plants.
Use tissue cultured materials, available fom
Monitoring: Observe the yellow streaks on the petiole (leaf stalk) of oldest, lower most leaves.
Affected leaves show progressive yellowing, break at the petiole and hang down along the pseudostem (Mother stem).
Observe the longitudinal splitting of pseudostem.
Cut a cross section of infected pseudostem and check for discoloured, reddish brown ring like lines.
Act immediately when after first symptoms observed.
Direct Control: As soon as symptoms are noticed the affected plants should be uprooted and burned along with the rhizome, roots and infected soil.
Restrictions: There are no chemical controls recommended for this disease.
